note.label: 1 Chronicles 14: David Established and Inquiring of the Most High

precepts.why:
“The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it unto thee, lest thou be snared therein: for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.” Their images are to be burned so they do not become a snare unto us.

David kept this. He smote the Philistines at Baal-perazim and said, “God hath broken in upon mine enemies by mine hand like the breaking forth of waters”, naming the place for it. “And when they had left their gods there, David gave a commandment, and they were burned with fire.”

precepts.text: The Most High is a man of war and knows exactly how to handle the battle.
precepts.point: David did exactly as commanded and smote them from Gibeon to Gazer. The lesson is precise obedience: if he says do not go up, do not go up; if he says go this way, do not go that way.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 14: David Established and Inquiring of the Most High

precepts.why:
“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.” The Most High is a man of war, and He knows exactly how to handle the battle.

When the Philistines came up a second time, David did not presume on the first victory; he “enquired again of God”. This time the Most High told him, “Go not up after them; turn away from them, and come upon them over against the mulberry trees.” He was to move only “when thou shalt hear a sound of going in the tops of the mulberry trees”, “for God is gone forth before thee to smite the host of the Philistines.” The man of war laid out the battle Himself and went before David.

precepts.text: Saul was told to overcome nations and did not, and was told not to go to his last battle yet went and died there; obedience is better than sacrifice.
precepts.point: David did exactly as commanded and smote them from Gibeon to Gazer. The lesson is precise obedience: if he says do not go up, do not go up; if he says go this way, do not go that way.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 14: David Established and Inquiring of the Most High

precepts.why:
“Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams. For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry.”

Saul was told to overcome nations and did not. He was told not to go to his last battle, yet he went and died there. “Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king.”

David is the other side of it: “David therefore did as God commanded him: and they smote the host of the Philistines from Gibeon even to Gazer.” The lesson is precise obedience. If he says do not go up, do not go up; if he says go this way, do not go that way.
